title: Profile of the bow and midship section of the Isabella
creator: John Ross
description: Construction diagrams showing how the Isabella and Alexander were strengthened for the ice: the doubled and fortified bow in profile and the midship section with its riders and shores. This is what "ice-strengthened" meant in 1818.

title: Coastal and ice view, facing p. 18
creator: after John Ross
description: An aquatint view of the ice on the outward passage, from Ross's own drawing.

title: Ice view, facing p. 46
creator: after John Ross
description: An aquatint of the ships among heavy floes and bergs in Davis Strait.

title: Coloured view of the bay with icebergs, facing p. 50
creator: after John Ross
description: A hand-coloured aquatint of a bay on the Greenland shore, a ship lying under the land among grounded bergs.

title: An inhabitant of the west coast of Greenland
creator: after John Sacheuse
description: Hand-coloured plate of a Greenlander seated in a doorway. Ross's Greenlandic interpreter John Sacheuse drew several of the human subjects in this book, which makes them among the earliest published images of Greenlanders by a Greenlander.

title: Ice cliff, facing p. 58
creator: after John Ross
description: An aquatint of a great ice cliff with the ships below for scale.

title: Iceberg, facing p. 74
creator: after John Ross
description: An aquatint of a large berg in Baffin Bay.

title: First communication with the natives of Prince Regent's Bay, drawn by John Sacheuse
creator: John Sacheuse
description: The plate Ross's own caption credits to John Sacheuse, who drew it and presented it to Ross on 10 August 1818: the meeting on the ice with the Inughuit of north-west Greenland, a people who until that day believed themselves alone in the world. Sacheuse, a Greenlander, is the interpreter standing between the two parties, and he is the artist - an Indigenous eyewitness account of first contact, published as a plate.

title: Arctic Highlander
creator: after John Sacheuse
description: Hand-coloured full-length portrait of one of the Inughuit Ross called Arctic Highlanders, in a full suit of skin clothing with high boots.

title: Natural history plate, facing p. 102
creator: after John Ross
description: A plate of specimens collected on the voyage, engraved for the narrative.

title: Chart of the coast, facing p. 116
creator: John Ross
description: A coloured chart of the coast surveyed by the Isabella and Alexander, with the ships' track laid down.

title: The Crimson Cliffs, with coloured snow
creator: after John Ross
description: Hand-coloured plate of the cliffs near Cape York whose snow is stained deep red. Ross brought samples home and the colour was traced to a microscopic alga, Chlamydomonas nivalis - one of the first biological discoveries of nineteenth-century Arctic exploration, and still a subject of study on this coast.

title: Coastal panorama, facing p. 143
creator: after John Ross
description: A long panoramic strip of the coastline as seen from the ship, drawn to fix the outline of new land.

title: Ice view, facing p. 160
creator: after John Ross
description: An aquatint of the pack in Baffin Bay.

title: Ice view, facing p. 170
creator: after John Ross
description: An aquatint of bergs and floes.

title: Coastal view, facing p. 192
creator: after John Ross
description: A framed coastal view from the western side of Baffin Bay.

title: Panoramic coastal profile, facing p. 192
creator: after John Ross
description: A panoramic profile strip of the land at the entrance to Lancaster Sound - the coast across which Ross believed he saw a range of mountains closing the sound, the "Croker Mountains" that were not there and that cost him his reputation.

title: Ice view, facing p. 208
creator: after John Ross
description: An aquatint of the ships in the ice late in the voyage.

title: Diagrams of the deviation of the compass in H.M.S. Isabella
creator: Edward Sabine and John Ross
description: Diagram No. 1, showing the deviation of the Isabella's compass obtained by actual observation on every point, with Diagram No. 2 for the same at Shetland. Iron in the hull throws the compass off, and quantifying that error was one of the voyage's real scientific results.

title: Diagrams of the deviation of the compass in H.M.S. Alexander
creator: Edward Sabine and John Ross
description: Diagram No. 3, the Alexander's deviation on 27 July in lat. 75d30'N, long. 60dW, with Diagram No. 4 for the same ship at Lerwick - the deviation measured in high latitudes against the deviation measured at home.

title: Appendix No. II: Zoological memoranda
creator: John Ross
description: The opening of the zoological appendix, listing the animals taken and observed on the voyage.

title: Appendix No. III: Geological memoranda
creator: John Ross
description: The opening of the geological appendix on the rocks collected along Baffin Bay.

title: Specimens from Agnes Monument, lat. 70d37'N, long. 67d50'W
creator: John Ross
description: The list of rock specimens from one collecting locality - granite, gneiss, greywacke schist - with its latitude and longitude, the format of a nineteenth-century field record.

title: Table of latitudes and longitudes
creator: John Ross
description: The appendix table of observed positions through the voyage, paired latitude and longitude down the page.

title: Observations on the pendulum, furnished by Mr J. C. Ross
creator: James Clark Ross
description: Pendulum observations contributed by James Clark Ross, then a midshipman on his first Arctic voyage, for the determination of the figure of the earth. He would go on to fix the North Magnetic Pole in 1831.

title: Botanical appendix, by Robert Brown, F.R.S.
creator: Robert Brown
description: The botanical appendix contributed by Robert Brown, librarian to Sir Joseph Banks and the most eminent botanist of his day, describing the plants collected on the shores of Baffin Bay.

title: List of plants collected on the voyage
creator: Robert Brown
description: Brown's list of the plants gathered on the Greenland and Baffin Island shores - the first systematic Arctic plant collection from this coast to reach European science.

title: Meteorological register of His Majesty's Ship Isabella
creator: John Ross
description: The large folding meteorological register of the Isabella's voyage of discovery in the Arctic regions, 1818: the daily record of barometer, thermometer, wind and weather, ruled across the whole opened sheet.

title: Panoramic coastal profiles
creator: after John Ross
description: A sheet of panoramic coastal profiles at the end of the volume, the sailing-directions form in which a navigator recorded what a new coast looks like from seaward.
